html:
The Tepehuán are a Native American people of the Sierra Madre Occidental in Durango and Chihuahua, in northern Mexico. They speak Uto-Aztecan languages related to those of the Pima.

They farmed and hunted in the mountain valleys. Spanish miners and ranchers moved into their land from the 1560s, and Jesuit missions followed. In 1616 a prophet led the Tepehuán Revolt, which killed several missionaries and many Spanish settlers and threatened the whole north of New Spain. Spain needed some years to put it down.

Their neighbours in the Sierra included the Acaxee and Xixime. The Tepehuán survive today in two main branches, northern and southern. See also Tepehuán on the modern map.
sum: The Tepehuán are a Native American people of the Sierra Madre Occidental in Durango and Chihuahua, in northern Mexico. They speak Uto-Aztecan languages related to those of the Pima.
